newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi governor sets state address for Jan 14.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi governor sets state address for Jan 14.

text.p: Mississippi Gov. Kirk Fordice has tentavely scheduled his state-of-the-state address for Jan 14, an aide said Monday.

The address will come a week after the Mississippi legislature opens its 90-day annual session Tuesday. Fordice, who usually addresses lawmakers on the opening day of the session, is still recovering from a November car crash.
He is expected to ask lawmakers for cuts in the state income tax, including a repeal the "marriage pe nalty" that taxes married couples at a higher rate than two single people with the same incomes.
The proposal would cost state coffers about $10 million the first year. About half of Mississippi's 920,000 state income tax payers are married.
Fordice's proposal would raise the personal exemption for married couples from $9,500 to $12,00 over three years. The exemption for single taxpayers would remain at $6,000.
Although the legislative session opens Tuesday, little formal business is expected until after Jan 20, the deadline to introduce general bills and constitutional amendments.
